title: Skill
description: An invocable procedure, and the unit at which an agent acts on the substrate; admissible only if it declares name, preconditions, body, postconditions, and witness format.
$comment: A skill is an invocable procedure, and it is the unit at which an agent acts on the substrate. Its admissibility condition is exact: a skill entity carries predications declaring its name, its preconditions, its body, its postconditions, and its witness format — 'a skill that does not declare these is not admissible, the invocation cannot be checked against its specification.' That is the Hoare triple as a gate, not as prose: pre-invocation the invocation operator checks the preconditions match; post-invocation it checks the postconditions hold. Skills are first-class entities, not registry entries: 'a new skill is added by inserting a skill entity, not by recompiling', and discovery is a substrate traversal of capability predications. A skill sits at the third rung of the formality progression observation -> instinct -> skill -> tool; it is the office's constructor, and constructors are the one component of an office that is universally F3-formal.

name.$comment: Equals the containing directory's basename. The harness resolves the skill by this name; a mismatch installs a skill nobody can invoke by the name they read.

verb-phrase.$comment: The gerund phrase naming the act — 'recalling a term', 'installing claude as an office'. Not decoration and not style: a skill is what an agent DOES, and the gerund is what makes the name an act rather than a thing. This is why the live skills are named as they are.

description.$comment: What it does and when to use it. The only field the harness shows before the body loads, so it carries the whole triggering decision, written for a blank incumbent with no access to emsenn's judgment.

preconditions.$comment: P — what must hold before invocation is admissible, as predicate patterns over the substrate. Checked by the invocation operator, not by the incumbent remembering. minItems 1: a skill with no stated precondition claims it is admissible everywhere, and nothing that touches the substrate is.

postconditions.$comment: Q — what the skill ensures is present after successful completion. Checked post-invocation. minItems 1: a skill ensuring nothing did nothing.

witness.$comment: The witness format. Every invocation produces one — which agent invoked the skill, on what scope, with what input, with what output — appended to the event log, so a replay reproduces the invocation and an audit verifies it. Required by the admissibility condition.

closure-kind.$comment: Which of the nuclear quartet's positions the body occupies: sigma (closure against the past) and delta (closure against the future), each at fixed point or open. process = both fixed, byte-identical replay. derivation = sigma open. procedure = delta open, routes. inquiry = both open, non-deterministic by design. Exclusive — an operation that crosses positions has been mis-specified, and the discipline is to split it. Distinct from a phase signature: closure-kind is which closure operators have settled, phase is the settling dynamics.

provides-capability.$comment: What invoking this skill makes available. Read by eligibility-by-capabilities at dispatch.

requires-capabilities.$comment: The capabilities the invoker must hold. Checked against the dispatchable's held set; this is where the skill layer and the capability layer actually meet.

script.$comment: The body's entrypoint, relative to the skill directory. Repo-relative or absolute paths are refused: the whole directory copies on install, so a path reaching outside it names a file the incumbent will not have.

fuel.$comment: The hard cap. An inquiry is bounded ONLY by the substrate's fuel discipline applied as a hard cap.

allOf.$comment: A process produces identical output for identical input and contains no conditional: it cannot be bound to an inference model, and its body must be a script, because prose cannot owe that contract.
An inquiry is non-deterministic by design and bounded only by fuel.
A derivation produces a typed judgment by fixed rules or reports it could reach none; sigma-open is not delta-open, so it takes no fuel cap.

$comment-absences: No duty key, no office key, no position key: a skill does not name what bears it. An office's provides-skill list and its deontic profile are where the relation lives — an agent's provided set is 'the union of its directly-listed skills plus the skills its offices' duties qualify it to invoke.' No contract key: the preconditions, postconditions, and witness ARE the contract, declared here because the admissibility condition requires them on the skill entity itself. No registry key: the substrate is the registry — 'there is no separate registry, no compiled list of available skills, no service layer that mediates skill discovery.'
